_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 1.8 (Code D). No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027 y Code D vigente.

questions.scenario: SHAW is arrested for a street robbery. He denies being the robber. The victim saw the robber for about 10 seconds and gave a description. SHAW is in custody and willing to take part. What should normally happen?
options: An identification procedure should be held, normally a video identification
Nothing – the victim's description is enough
The victim should be shown SHAW alone in the custody suite
The victim should look through mugshot albums
explanations: Correct: known, available, disputes, witness may identify.
Incorrect: Code D requires a procedure in these circumstances.
Photos are only shown when the suspect is not known.
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 1.8 · When a procedure must be held

questions.scenario: When is a suspect 'known' for the purposes of Code D?
options: When a witness has picked them out
When there is sufficient information to justify their arrest for suspected involvement

questions.scenario: A victim tells police she was assaulted by her husband of 12 years, who denies being there. Is an identification procedure required?
options: Yes, always when identity is disputed
No, it would serve no useful purpose because the victim knows him well
Yes, a confrontation must be used
Only if the husband requests it

questions.scenario: Who should normally be responsible for arranging and conducting an identification procedure?
options: An identification officer not below the rank of inspector who is not involved in the investigation
explanations: Investigating officers must not be involved.

questions.scenario: Which is normally the first choice of eyewitness identification procedure when the suspect is known and available?
explanations: Only when the suspect is not known.

questions.scenario: In a video identification, the images of the suspect must be shown with images of at least how many other people who resemble the suspect?
explanations: Correct (⚠ check Code D Annex A).
Twelve applies in some parade situations with two suspects.

questions.scenario: Which identification procedure involves the witness seeing ONLY the suspect?
A suspect refuses to take part in any identification procedure. Which may be used?
options: A covert procedure, such as covert video identification or group identification
Force to make him stand in a parade
explanations: Force cannot be used for a parade.

questions.scenario: Five minutes after a street robbery, the suspect is unknown. PC DIAZ drives the victim around the area to see if she can spot the robber. Which is correct?
options: It is allowed, but the officer must not direct the victim's attention to any individual and the first description should be recorded
The officer should point out likely suspects
Only allowed with an inspector's authority
explanations: It is allowed when the suspect is not known.
Incorrect – that would taint the identification.

questions.scenario: When may a witness be shown photographs (e.g. albums) to try to identify a suspect?
options: Only when the identity of the suspect is not known

questions.scenario: Which of the following is a NON-intimate sample?
options: A swab taken from the mouth

questions.scenario: What is required before an intimate sample is taken from a person in police detention?
options: Authorisation by an inspector (or above) and the person's written consent

questions.scenario: A suspect refuses, without good cause, to give an intimate sample. Which is correct?
options: Force can be used to take it
It is automatically a criminal offence
The court may draw such inferences from the refusal as appear proper
Nothing can follow from the refusal
explanations: Force cannot be used for intimate samples.

questions.scenario: Which of the following is an INTIMATE sample?
explanations: Correct: a swab from a body orifice other than the mouth.

questions.scenario: A man is arrested for a recordable offence and refuses to give his fingerprints. His prints have not been taken during this investigation. Which is correct?
options: Fingerprints can never be taken without consent
Only an inspector can take them
They can only be taken after conviction
Fingerprints may be taken without consent in these circumstances, using reasonable force if necessary

questions.scenario: Who must take a dental impression?
Why must the witness's first description be recorded?
options: So it can be compared with the suspect and disclosed, helping assess the reliability of the identification

questions.scenario: When must a judge give a Turnbull warning?
options: When the case depends wholly or substantially on disputed eyewitness identification
Only if the defendant has no lawyer

questions.scenario: Which of these is part of ADVOKATE?
options: Amount of time the witness saw the suspect

questions.scenario: Officers are shown CCTV of a burglary to see if any of them recognise the suspect. Which is correct?
options: They should all watch together and discuss names
Code D has rules for recognition from images, e.g. recording how they recognise the person
explanations: It does apply (⚠ check Part B).

questions.scenario: Which statement about group identification is correct?
options: The witness sees the suspect in an informal group of people, and it can be held covertly
It can only take place in a police station
explanations: It often takes place in public places.

questions.scenario: Before an identification procedure, what must the suspect be told (in general)?
options: The purpose and procedure, their right to free legal advice, that refusal may be given in evidence, and that covert procedures may be used
Only the name of the witness
explanations: Correct (⚠ check the full list in Code D).

questions.scenario: A suspect is 'available' for Code D purposes when…
options: they are immediately available or will be within a reasonably short time, and willing to take part

questions.scenario: Can officers involved in the investigation take part in conducting the identification procedure?
options: No – they must not take part

questions.scenario: Where there are several witnesses and one makes a street identification, what should normally happen with the others?
options: They should be kept separate and, where possible, take part in a formal identification procedure
They should also be shown the person in the street
They should be told who was identified
They should be released as witnesses

questions.scenario: Which section of PACE allows the court to exclude identification evidence obtained in breach of Code D?
Which statement about photographs of detained persons (PACE s. 64A) is correct?
options: They can never be taken without consent
They can be taken with or without consent
explanations: Correct (⚠ check rules on force and removal of items).

questions.scenario: A footwear impression may be taken without consent from a person arrested for a recordable offence (if not already taken in the investigation) under which section?
The dispute in a case is not about who was present but about what happened (the suspect admits being there). Is an identification procedure likely to be required?
options: No, it would serve no useful purpose
Only if there are CCTV images

questions.scenario: Checking a suspect's fingerprints or DNA against national databases is known as…
